question: After selling an article at a discount of 25%, the profit percentage obtained is 2%. What is the mark-up percentage?
solution:
**Given:**

Discount = 25%

Profit = 2%

**Formula used:**

Mark-up percentage = ({Selling Price} - {Cost Price}) / {Cost Price} times 100

Selling Price = Marked Price - Discount

Cost Price = Selling Price / (1 + frac{{Profit Percentage}}{100})

**Calculations:**

Let Marked Price = ₹100

Discount = 25% of ₹100 = ₹25

⇒ Selling Price = ₹100 - ₹25 = ₹75

Profit = 2%, so Cost Price = Selling Price / (1 + (2)/(100))

⇒ Cost Price = ₹75 / 1.02 = ₹73.53

Mark-up percentage = ({Marked Price} - {Cost Price}) / {Cost Price} times 100

⇒ Mark-up percentage = (100 - 73.53) / 73.53 times 100

⇒ Mark-up percentage = (26.47 / 73.53) times 100

⇒ Mark-up percentage ≈ 36%

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**
